1	"""Single-file SQL query layer.
2	
3	Public API:
4	
5	* :func:`query_file` -- run a ``SELECT ... FROM input [WHERE ...]`` query
6	  against one columnar file and return a :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.Table`
7	* :func:`query_files` -- run a statement against a table-name to path
8	  mapping, optionally chaining several equi-joins
9	* :func:`explain_file` / :func:`explain_files` -- parse, bind and plan the
10	  same statements without executing them; only file metadata is read
11	* :class:`QuerySyntaxError` -- lexical / grammatical errors
12	* :class:`QueryValidationError` -- unknown columns, wrong table name,
13	  type-incompatible comparisons, invalid aggregate use
14	
15	The accepted grammar (keywords case-insensitive)::
16	
17	    query       := SELECT [DISTINCT] select_item (',' select_item)*
18	                   FROM ident [WHERE expr] [GROUP BY ident (',' ident)*]
19	                   [HAVING expr]
20	                   [ORDER BY order_item (',' order_item)*]
21	                   [LIMIT uint]
22	    select_item := '*' | ident | agg_name '(' [DISTINCT] ('*' | ident) ')'
23	                   | scalar_expr AS alias
24	    order_item  := (ident | agg_name '(' [DISTINCT] ('*' | ident) ')')
25	                   [ASC | DESC] [NULLS FIRST | NULLS LAST]
26	    expr       := or_expr
27	    or_expr     := and_expr (OR and_expr)*
28	    and_expr    := cmp_expr (AND cmp_expr)*
29	    cmp_expr    := not_factor (cmp_op not_factor)?
30	    not_factor  := NOT not_factor | postfix
31	    postfix     := scalar_expr (IS [NOT] NULL)?
32	    scalar_expr := term (('+' | '-') term)*
33	    term        := factor (('*' | '/') factor)*
34	    factor      := ('+' | '-') factor | atom
35	    atom        := '(' expr ')' | operand
36	                | CASE WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr
37	                  (WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr)*
38	                  (ELSE scalar_expr)? END
39	    operand     := ident | literal
40	    literal     := TRUE | FALSE | [+-]? int64 | [+-]? finite float64
41	                   | single-quoted utf8
42	
43	The supported aggregates are ``COUNT(*)``, ``COUNT(ident)`` and
44	``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` applied to one column.  Each of
45	``COUNT`` / ``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` also accepts
46	``DISTINCT`` before its single column argument (``COUNT(DISTINCT ident)``
47	etc.): rows are first selected by WHERE, then within each group (or the
48	single global group) NULL arguments are ignored and the remaining values
49	are deduplicated by the column's type -- float64 ``0.0`` and ``-0.0``
50	count as the same value -- before the aggregate runs.  ``COUNT(DISTINCT
51	x)`` returns the number of distinct non-NULL values (0 on empty input,
52	a non-nullable int64); the other DISTINCT aggregates return NULL when no
53	distinct non-NULL value remains and otherwise keep the result type,
54	nullability, comparison rules and overflow / non-finite
55	:class:`QueryValidationError` behaviour of their plain counterparts.
56	DISTINCT here only deduplicates the aggregate's argument values; it does
57	not change ``SELECT DISTINCT`` row deduplication, and the argument stays
58	a single column reference (no ``*``, expressions, multiple arguments or
59	nested aggregates).  A misplaced DISTINCT keyword, a missing argument,
60	``*``, an expression or multiple arguments inside a DISTINCT call raise
61	:class:`QuerySyntaxError` before any file is opened.  DISTINCT
62	aggregates may appear wherever plain aggregates may (SELECT, HAVING,
63	ORDER BY), and textually identical calls share one computation.  Without
64	GROUP BY the projection may contain aggregate expressions only; with
65	GROUP BY it may additionally contain the grouped columns.  A bare ``*``
66	must not be mixed with aggregates or grouping.  Aggregates are not
67	allowed inside WHERE, may not be nested, and aliases are not supported
68	for bare columns or aggregate calls.
69	
70	Scalar arithmetic (parentheses, unary ``+``/``-``, binary ``+`` ``-``
71	``*`` ``/``; precedence: parentheses, unary, ``*``/``/``, ``+``/``-``)
72	is available over int64 / float64 columns and numeric literals in SELECT
73	and WHERE.  A computed SELECT expression must be named with ``AS`` (the
74	alias follows the usual identifier rules and must be unique among the
75	output names); bare columns and aggregate calls keep their existing
76	result names.  int64 ``+``/``-``/``*`` on two int64 operands yields
77	int64; any float64 operand or a division yields float64, and unary
78	operators preserve the operand type.  Any NULL operand makes the result
79	NULL; the output column is nullable iff a participating column is
80	nullable (pure constants are not).  int64 overflow, division by zero and
81	non-finite float64 results raise :class:`QueryValidationError`.  A
82	numeric expression used directly as a boolean condition is rejected with
83	:class:`QueryValidationError` as well.  Non-aggregate queries execute
84	WHERE, then compute the sort keys, stably sort, apply LIMIT and only
85	then evaluate the SELECT expressions, so filtered or truncated rows
86	never trigger division-by-zero or overflow in the projection; a
87	DISTINCT query instead evaluates the projection right after WHERE,
88	deduplicates the result rows, and only then sorts and applies LIMIT.  ORDER BY
89	may name a SELECT alias (an alias shadows an input column of the same
90	name) and sorts on the expression's result type with the usual NULL
91	placement and stability rules.  Aggregate queries do not accept scalar
92	expressions: GROUP BY keys and aggregate arguments stay plain column
93	references, and mixing a scalar expression into an aggregate query
94	raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
95	
96	``SELECT DISTINCT`` removes duplicate rows from a non-aggregate query:
97	the projection may be a star, plain columns or ``AS``-aliased scalar
98	expressions exactly as without DISTINCT, and deduplication compares the
99	full projected result row column by column after WHERE.  Two NULLs in
100	the same result column compare equal, NULL never equals a non-NULL
101	value, bool / utf8 / numeric values keep their existing comparison
102	semantics, and float64 ``0.0`` and ``-0.0`` compare equal.  Without
103	ORDER BY the surviving rows keep the order of the first occurrence of
104	each distinct result row; ORDER BY then sorts the deduplicated rows and
105	LIMIT keeps the first N.  The projection expressions are evaluated
106	only for rows that passed WHERE (and, with ORDER BY, before the sort),
107	so a division by zero, int64 overflow or non-finite float64 result that
108	actually occurs still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.  ORDER BY
109	of a DISTINCT query may name only bare columns or explicit aliases that
110	are part of the projection; an unprojected or otherwise unknown name
111	raises :class:`QueryValidationError`, and the sort direction, NULL
112	placement and stability rules are unchanged.  DISTINCT combined with
113	GROUP BY, HAVING or any aggregate projection raises
114	:class:`QueryValidationError`; argument-level ``DISTINCT`` inside an
115	aggregate call (``COUNT(DISTINCT ...)`` etc.) is a separate feature
116	described above and stays an aggregate query.  A missing projection, a
117	repeated DISTINCT or a misplaced DISTINCT keyword raises
118	:class:`QuerySyntaxError` before any file is opened.
119	
120	Searched CASE expressions
121	(``CASE WHEN cond THEN result [WHEN ...] [ELSE result] END``; the simple
122	``CASE value WHEN ...`` form is not supported and at least one WHEN is
123	required) are scalar operands and may be nested inside more arithmetic,
124	comparisons and other CASE expressions.  For each row the WHEN conditions
125	are tested in written order and only TRUE matches; FALSE and UNKNOWN fall
126	through, an explicit ELSE supplies the fallback and a missing ELSE yields
127	NULL.  Only the chosen result is evaluated, so division by zero, int64
128	overflow or a non-finite float64 inside an unhit branch never raises; a
129	chosen result that errors still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
130	Every reachable THEN and an explicit ELSE must share one type family:
131	int64 and float64 may mix and unify to float64, while bool and utf8 must
132	match each other exactly (any other mix raises
133	:class:`QueryValidationError`).  The result column is nullable if any
134	reachable result is nullable or the ELSE is omitted.  WHEN conditions use
135	the same boolean type check and three-valued logic as WHERE; CASE stays a
136	scalar expression, so it is rejected in aggregate arguments, GROUP BY and
137	the projection of an aggregate query just like the other scalar
138	expressions.
139	
140	Operator precedence (highest first) is NOT, comparison, AND, OR; IS [NOT]
141	NULL is a postfix of its scalar operand.  Comparison operands may be
142	column references, literals or scalar arithmetic expressions.  WHERE
143	follows SQL three-valued logic: a normal
144	comparison against NULL yields UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN propagates through the
145	logical operators, and only TRUE rows are returned.
146	
147	After WHERE, rows are grouped in GROUP BY column order (a NULL key forms
148	its own group); without an explicit ORDER BY groups come out in the order
149	of their first selected row.  An optional HAVING clause between GROUP BY
150	and ORDER BY filters the formed groups with the same boolean expression
151	grammar and three-valued logic as WHERE: its conditions combine grouping
152	columns, aggregate calls and type-compatible literals with NOT / AND / OR
153	/ comparisons / IS [NOT] NULL, only groups whose condition is TRUE are
154	kept, and aggregates named in HAVING need not appear in SELECT.  Without
155	GROUP BY HAVING filters the single global aggregate row (still produced
156	when WHERE selected no rows); with GROUP BY an empty selection yields
157	zero groups.  HAVING may not name ungrouped plain columns, ``*``, CASE,
158	scalar arithmetic or nested aggregates; it is rejected on a completely
159	non-aggregate query.  ORDER BY may only name a selected result; ASC is the
160	default, NULLs sort last regardless of direction unless NULLS FIRST /
161	NULLS LAST is given, and groups equal on every sort key keep that
162	first-row order.  LIMIT then keeps the first N groups.  Without GROUP BY
163	and aggregates an aggregate query over zero selected rows still yields one
164	output row (COUNT 0, the other aggregates NULL), unless HAVING removes it;
165	with GROUP BY it yields zero rows.
166	
167	Multi-file queries (:func:`query_files`) add a deterministic chain of zero
168	or more equi-joins to the grammar::
169	
170	    query := SELECT ... FROM from_table
171	             { join_kind JOIN next_table
172	               ON (earlier_table.col = next_table.col
173	                   | next_table.col = earlier_table.col) } ...
174	    join_kind := INNER | LEFT | RIGHT | FULL OUTER
175	
176	``sources`` maps table names to file paths; only the tables referenced by
177	the statement are read.  Each join step introduces exactly one not-yet-used
178	table (aliases and repeated tables are rejected) and its single ON equality
179	connects a qualified column of that new table with a qualified column of any
180	table introduced earlier (FROM or a previous join); the two sides of the
181	equality are interchangeable.  Compound or non-equality ON conditions,
182	other join types and ``FULL`` without ``OUTER`` are syntax errors raised
183	before any file is opened.  In any statement that contains a JOIN every
184	column reference outside ``COUNT(*)`` must be qualified as ``table.column``
185	(either part may be a double-quoted identifier).  ``SELECT *`` emits the
186	referenced schemas in FROM/JOIN order with ``table.column`` names; explicit
187	projections keep their qualified names and aggregates keep the uppercase
188	``FUNC(table.column)`` labels.
189	
190	Each step is evaluated with the materialised intermediate result as its
191	left input and the newly read table as its right input.  Join keys may
192	share a type or mix int64 with float64; NULL keys never match.  INNER JOIN
193	emits every matching combination, LEFT JOIN also emits unmatched left rows
194	with the right-side values set to NULL (the new table's result columns are
195	nullable), RIGHT JOIN emits all new-table rows in new-file order (one new
196	row's matches expand in intermediate/current row order) padding the whole
197	intermediate side with NULL (every earlier table's result columns become
198	nullable), and FULL OUTER JOIN emits the LEFT JOIN output and then appends
199	the unmatched new rows in new-file order (every result column is nullable).
200	INNER / LEFT / FULL expand in the current intermediate row order, with the
201	matching new rows in new-file order within one current row; RIGHT expands
202	in new-file row order with the matches in current row order.  Nullability
203	is derived per step: once a step makes an earlier table's columns
204	nullable, later steps keep them nullable.  WHERE / GROUP BY / HAVING /
205	projection / DISTINCT / stable sorting / LIMIT run only after the whole
206	chain has been built, with their usual semantics.
207	
208	The multi-file entry points (:func:`query_files`, :func:`explain_files`)
209	take an optional ``join_strategy`` of ``"hash"`` or ``"sort_merge"``; an
210	explicit strategy is applied to every join step.  Both strategies accept
211	the same statements and return identical column descriptions, values, NULL
212	placement and row order; they differ only in how matching right rows are
213	located (a right-key hash index versus sorting both sides on the key and
214	merging equal-key runs).  With the argument omitted the historical
215	default join path is used and the explain plan carries no strategy field;
216	with an explicit strategy every plan Join operator gains a ``strategy``
217	field of ``HASH`` or ``SORT_MERGE``.  A JOIN-less statement accepts either
218	strategy but gains no extra operator, and an invalid strategy raises
219	:class:`ValueError` before any source file is opened.
220	
221	The explain plan lists the referenced sources and their Scan operators in
222	FROM/JOIN order with ``required_columns`` attributed to each source, then
223	one Join operator per step in the same order, recording the step type and
224	the two normalised qualified keys (the earlier table on the left, the
225	freshly introduced table on the right).
226	
227	Row-group-partitioned (v2) files are read selectively: every query decodes
228	only the column blocks its plan actually references (a join chain
229	additionally reads each table's ON keys), and single-file statements --
230	:func:`query_file` and JOIN-less :func:`query_files` -- push the
231	AND-connected, type-compatible comparisons and IS [NOT] NULL conditions of
232	WHERE down to the per-group statistics.  A row group is skipped only when
233	its statistics prove the pushed condition can never be TRUE for any of its
234	rows; OR, NOT, CASE, arithmetic, column-to-column comparisons and
235	undecidable ranges keep the group, and surviving rows are still filtered
236	row by row with the full WHERE condition.  When every group is excluded
237	the statement simply sees zero rows, so empty results, ``COUNT(*)``, other
238	global aggregates and HAVING keep their usual semantics.  Both format
239	versions return identical column descriptions, values, row order, sorting,
240	LIMIT, join and export results for the same data and statement.  In the
241	explain plan a v2 single-source Scan operator additionally carries
242	``row_groups_total``, ``row_groups_selected`` and ``pushed_condition``
243	(the pushed-down subset of the WHERE condition as a condition tree, or
244	null); v1 plans are unchanged.

365	_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(
366	    r"""
367	    \d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?   # 1, 1., 1.5, 1e3, 1.5e-2
368	    | \.\d+(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?         # .5
369	    """,
370	    re.VERBOSE,
371	)
372	# Bare identifiers: Unicode letters/underscore first, then word characters.
373	_IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\W\d]\w*", re.UNICODE)
374	
375	
376	def _tokenize(sql: str) -> list[_Token]:
377	    if not isinstance(sql, str):
378	        raise QuerySyntaxError("SQL statement must be a string")
379	    tokens: list[_Token] = []
380	    i = 0
381	    n = len(sql)
382	    while i < n:
383	        ch = sql[i]
384	        if ch.isspace():
385	            i += 1
386	            continue
387	        if ch == "*":
388	            tokens.append(_Token("star", None, ch))
389	            i += 1
390	            continue
391	        if ch in ",()+-/":
392	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
393	            i += 1
394	            continue
395	        if ch in "=<>!":
396	            if ch == "!" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
397	                tokens.append(_Token("op", "!=", "!="))
398	                i += 2
399	                continue
400	            if ch in "<>" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
401	                op = ch + "="
402	                tokens.append(_Token("op", op, op))
403	                i += 2
404	                continue
405	            if ch in "=<>":
406	                tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
407	                i += 1
408	                continue
409	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character '!' at position {i}")
410	        if ch == "'":
411	            value, new_i = _tokenize_string(sql, i)
412	            tokens.append(_Token("string", value, sql[i:new_i]))
413	            i = new_i
414	            continue
415	        if ch == '"':
416	            value, new_i = _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql, i)
417	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(value, quoted=True))
418	            i = new_i
419	            continue
420	        if ch.isdigit() or ch == ".":
421	            match = _NUMBER_RE.match(sql, i)
422	            if match:
423	                text = match.group(0)
424	                tokens.append(_Token("number", _parse_number(text), text))
425	                i = match.end()
426	                continue
427	            # A '.' that does not start a number is the qualifier separator
428	            # used by multi-table queries ("table.column").
429	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ".", ch))
430	            i += 1
431	            continue
432	        match = _IDENT_RE.match(sql, i)
433	        if match:
434	            text = match.group(0)
435	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(text, quoted=False))
436	            i = match.end()
437	            continue
438	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character {ch!r} at position {i}")
439	    tokens.append(_Token("eof", None, ""))
440	    return tokens
441	
442	
443	def _token_from_word(word: str, *, quoted: bool) -> _Token:
444	    lowered = word.lower()
445	    if not quoted and lowered in _KEYWORDS:
446	        if lowered == "true":
447	            return _Token("number", True, word)
448	        if lowered == "false":
449	            return _Token("number", False, word)
450	        return _Token("keyword", lowered, word)
451	    return _Token("qident" if quoted else "ident", word, word)
452	
453	
454	def _tokenize_string(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
455	    parts: list[str] = []
456	    i = start + 1
457	    n = len(sql)
458	    while True:
459	        j = sql.find("'", i)
460	        if j == -1:
461	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated string literal")
462	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
463	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == "'":
464	            parts.append("'")
465	            i = j + 2
466	            continue
467	        value = "".join(parts)
468	        try:
469	            value.encode("utf-8")
470	        except UnicodeEncodeError:
471	            raise QuerySyntaxError("string literal is not valid UTF-8") from None
472	        return value, j + 1
473	
474	
475	def _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
476	    parts: list[str] = []
477	    i = start + 1
478	    n = len(sql)
479	    while True:
480	        j = sql.find('"', i)
481	        if j == -1:
482	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated quoted identifier")
483	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
484	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == '"':
485	            parts.append('"')
486	            i = j + 2
487	            continue
488	        value = "".join(parts)
489	        if not value:
490	            raise QuerySyntaxError("quoted identifier must not be empty")
491	        return value, j + 1
492	
493	
494	def _parse_number(text: str) -> int | float:
495	    try:
496	        if any(ch in text for ch in ".eE"):
497	            value: int | float = float(text)
498	        else:
499	            value = int(text, 10)
500	    except ValueError:
501	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"invalid numeric literal {text!r}") from None
502	    if isinstance(value, int):
503	        # The magnitude 2**63 is accepted unsigned; the signed range check
504	        # happens after the optional leading sign is applied.
505	        if not (0 <= value <= 2**63):
506	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"integer literal {text} is outside the int64 range")
507	        return value
508	    if not math.isfinite(value):
509	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"float literal {text} must be finite")
510	    return value

513	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
514	# Parsed expression tree
515	#
516	# Node tuples:
517	#   ("literal", python_value, type_name)
518	#   ("column", name, table|None, table_quoted)        -- as parsed
519	#   ("column", name, index, type_name, nullable)      -- after binding
520	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node)              -- as parsed (+ - * /)
521	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node, type_name)   -- after binding
522	#   ("unary", operand, negate)                        -- as parsed
523	#   ("unary", operand, negate, type_name)             -- after binding
524	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None)   -- as parsed
525	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None, type_name) -- after binding
526	#   ("cmp", op, left_node, right_node)
527	#   ("isnull", operand, negate)
528	#   ("not", operand)
529	#   ("and"|"or", left, right)
530	# Predicate nodes are boolean-typed (three-valued at evaluation time);
531	# "literal"/"column"/"arith"/"unary" nodes are value nodes.
532	#
533	# Projection / ORDER BY reference items:
534	#   ("column_ref", name)                 -- a plain column name
535	#   ("agg", func_upper, arg_name|None)   -- an aggregate call; arg None = '*'
536	#   ("expr", alias)                      -- a computed scalar expression
537	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
538	
539	
540	@dataclass(frozen=True)
541	class _RefItem:
542	    """One projection element or ORDER BY key as parsed."""
543	
544	    kind: str  # "star" | "column" | "agg" | "expr"
545	    name: str | None = None  # column name, or the AS alias for kind == "expr"
546	    func: str | None = None  # uppercase function name for kind == "agg"
547	    arg: str | None = None  # aggregate column argument; "" stands for '*'
548	    distinct: bool = False  # kind == "agg": DISTINCT before the argument
549	    expr: tuple | None = None  # parsed scalar expression for kind == "expr"
550	    descending: bool = False
551	    nulls_first: bool | None = None  # None -> default (NULLs last)
552	    # Table qualifiers (multi-table queries only; None when unqualified):
553	    table: str | None = None
554	    table_quoted: bool = False
555	    arg_table: str | None = None
556	    arg_table_quoted: bool = False
557	
558	
559	@dataclass(frozen=True)
560	class _Join:
561	    """One equi-join step of a multi-table query.
562	
563	    A statement may chain several steps in FROM/JOIN order; each step takes
564	    the intermediate result built so far as its left input and one freshly
565	    introduced table as its right input.
566	    """
567	
568	    kind: str  # "inner" | "left" | "right" | "full"
569	    table: str  # right table name as spelled
570	    table_quoted: bool
571	    left_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
572	    right_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
573	
574	
575	@dataclass
576	class _Select:
577	    items: tuple[_RefItem, ...]  # projection; may be a single ("star",) item
578	    table: str
579	    table_quoted: bool
580	    where: tuple | None
581	    # GROUP BY entries are (table|None, table_quoted, name) triples.
582	    group_by: tuple[tuple, ...] | None
583	    # Post-grouping boolean expression (aggregate queries only); None absent.
584	    having: tuple | None
585	    order_by: tuple[_RefItem, ...] | None
586	    limit: int | None
587	    # Join steps in FROM/JOIN order; empty for a single-table statement.
588	    joins: tuple[_Join, ...] = ()
589	    # SELECT DISTINCT: deduplicate the projected rows (non-aggregate only).
590	    distinct: bool = False
591	
592	    @property
593	    def star(self) -> bool:
594	        return len(self.items) == 1 and self.items[0].kind == "star"
595	
596	    @property
597	    def has_aggregate(self) -> bool:
598	        return any(item.kind == "agg" for item in self.items)
599	
600	    @property
601	    def is_aggregate_query(self) -> bool:
602	        return self.has_aggregate or self.group_by is not None or self.having is not None
603	
604	
605	class _Parser:
606	    _CMP_OPS = frozenset(("=", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">="))
607	
608	    def __init__(self, tokens: list[_Token], allow_join: bool = False):
609	        self.tokens = tokens
610	        self.pos = 0
611	        # Multi-table statements (qualified names + join clauses) are only
612	        # enabled for query_files; single-file entry points keep rejecting
613	        # them as syntax errors.
614	        self._allow_join = allow_join
615	
616	    def parse(self) -> _Select:
617	        select = self._parse_select()
618	        if self._peek().kind != "eof":
619	            tok = self._peek()
620	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected trailing input {tok.text!r}")
621	        return select
622	
623	    def _parse_select(self) -> _Select:
624	        self._expect_keyword("select")
625	        distinct = self._accept_keyword("distinct")
626	        items = tuple(self._parse_projection())
627	        self._expect_keyword("from")
628	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
629	        joins: tuple[_Join, ...] = ()
630	        if self._allow_join:
631	            joins = tuple(self._parse_join_clauses())
632	        where = None
633	        if self._accept_keyword("where"):
634	            where = self._parse_or()
635	        group_by = None
636	        if self._accept_keyword("group"):
637	            self._expect_keyword("by")
638	            names = [self._parse_group_name()]
639	            while self._accept_op(","):
640	                names.append(self._parse_group_name())
641	            group_by = tuple(names)
642	        having = None
643	        if self._accept_keyword("having"):
644	            having = self._parse_having_or()
645	        order_by = None
646	        if self._accept_keyword("order"):
647	            self._expect_keyword("by")
648	            order_items = [self._parse_order_item()]
649	            while self._accept_op(","):
650	                order_items.append(self._parse_order_item())
651	            order_by = tuple(order_items)
652	        limit = None
653	        if self._accept_keyword("limit"):
654	            limit = self._parse_limit()
655	        return _Select(
656	            items=items,
657	            table=table_tok.value,
658	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
659	            where=where,
660	            group_by=group_by,
661	            having=having,
662	            order_by=order_by,
663	            limit=limit,
664	            joins=joins,
665	            distinct=distinct,
666	        )
667	
668	    def _parse_join_clauses(self) -> list[_Join]:
669	        # Zero or more join clauses may follow FROM; each introduces exactly
670	        # one new table with a single equi-ON condition.  "right" / "full" /
671	        # "outer" stay ordinary identifiers away from this clause (they are
672	        # matched with _accept_word), so columns carrying those names keep
673	        # working outside join parsing.
674	        joins: list[_Join] = []
675	        while True:
676	            if self._accept_keyword("inner"):
677	                self._expect_keyword("join")
678	                joins.append(self._parse_join("inner"))
679	            elif self._accept_keyword("left"):
680	                self._expect_keyword("join")
681	                joins.append(self._parse_join("left"))
682	            elif self._accept_word("right"):
683	                self._expect_keyword("join")
684	                joins.append(self._parse_join("right"))
685	            elif self._accept_word("full"):
686	                # Only the explicit FULL OUTER JOIN spelling is accepted.
687	                self._expect_word("outer")
688	                self._expect_keyword("join")
689	                joins.append(self._parse_join("full"))
690	            else:
691	                return joins
692	
693	    def _parse_join(self, kind: str) -> _Join:
694	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
695	        self._expect_keyword("on")
696	        left_key = self._parse_on_key()
697	        self._expect_op("=")
698	        right_key = self._parse_on_key()
699	        return _Join(
700	            kind=kind,
701	            table=table_tok.value,
702	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
703	            left_key=left_key,
704	            right_key=right_key,
705	        )
706	
707	    def _parse_on_key(self) -> tuple:
708	        tok = self._peek()
709	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
710	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
711	                f"ON requires table-qualified columns, got {tok.text!r}"
712	            )
713	        self._next()
714	        if not self._accept_op("."):
715	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
716	                "ON requires table-qualified columns (table.column)"
717	            )
718	        nxt = self._peek()
719	        if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
720	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
721	                f"expected column name after '.' in ON, got {nxt.text!r}"
722	            )
723	        self._next()
724	        return (tok.value, tok.kind == "qident", nxt.value)
725	
726	    def _parse_projection(self) -> list[_RefItem]:
727	        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
728	        while self._accept_op(","):
729	            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
730	        # Aliases are only supported for computed scalar expressions (which
731	        # consume their own "AS alias" in _parse_select_item); a trailing
732	        # identifier (including the spelling "as") where FROM is expected
733	        # names one on a bare column or aggregate.  Plain queries keep their
734	        # historical QuerySyntaxError classification; aggregate queries treat
735	        # the unsupported alias as a validation error.
736	        tok = self._peek()
737	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident") or (
738	            tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "as"
739	        ):
740	            grouped_ahead = any(
741	                t.kind == "keyword" and t.value == "group"
742	                for t in self.tokens[self.pos :]
743	            )
744	            if any(item.kind == "agg" for item in items) or grouped_ahead:
745	                raise QueryValidationError(
746	                    f"aliases are not supported; unexpected {tok.text!r} after projection item"
747	                )
748	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected FROM, got {tok.text!r}")
749	        return items
750	
751	    def _parse_select_item(self) -> _RefItem:
752	        tok = self._peek()
753	        if tok.kind == "star":
754	            self._next()
755	            return _RefItem("star")
756	        if (
757	            tok.kind == "ident"
758	            and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
759	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
760	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
761	        ):
762	            item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
763	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
764	                raise QueryValidationError(
765	                    "aggregate calls cannot be combined with scalar arithmetic"
766	                )
767	            return item
768	        node = self._parse_arith()
769	        if node[0] == "column":
770	            # A bare (possibly parenthesised) column reference keeps its
771	            # existing projection behaviour and needs no alias.
772	            return _RefItem(
773	                "column", name=node[1], table=node[2], table_quoted=node[3]
774	            )
775	        # A computed scalar expression must be named with AS.
776	        self._expect_keyword("as")
777	        alias = self._peek()
778	        if alias.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
779	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
780	                f"AS requires a result name, got {alias.text!r}"
781	            )
782	        self._next()
783	        return _RefItem("expr", name=alias.value, expr=node)
784	
785	    def _arith_op_ahead(self) -> bool:
786	        tok = self._peek()
787	        return tok.kind == "star" or (
788	            tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-", "/")
789	        )
790	
791	    def _parse_order_item(self) -> _RefItem:
792	        item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
793	        descending = False
794	        if self._accept_keyword("asc"):
795	            descending = False
796	        elif self._accept_keyword("desc"):
797	            descending = True
798	        nulls_first: bool | None = None
799	        if self._accept_keyword("nulls"):
800	            if self._accept_keyword("first"):
801	                nulls_first = True
802	            elif self._accept_keyword("last"):
803	                nulls_first = False
804	            else:
805	                tok = self._peek()
806	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
807	                    f"expected FIRST or LAST after NULLS, got {tok.text!r}"
808	                )
809	        return _RefItem(
810	            item.kind,
811	            name=item.name,
812	            func=item.func,
813	            arg=item.arg,
814	            distinct=item.distinct,
815	            descending=descending,
816	            nulls_first=nulls_first,
817	            table=item.table,
818	            table_quoted=item.table_quoted,
819	            arg_table=item.arg_table,
820	            arg_table_quoted=item.arg_table_quoted,
821	        )
822	
823	    def _qualifier_ahead(self) -> bool:
824	        nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
825	        return nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "."
826	
827	    def _parse_qualified_column(self) -> _RefItem:
828	        # Current token starts "table.column"; consumes all three tokens.
829	        table_tok = self._next()
830	        self._expect_op(".")
831	        name_tok = self._peek()
832	        if name_tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
833	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
834	                f"expected identifier after '.', got {name_tok.text!r}"
835	            )
836	        self._next()
837	        return _RefItem(
838	            "column",
839	            name=name_tok.value,
840	            table=table_tok.value,
841	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
842	        )
843	
844	    def _parse_column_or_agg(self) -> _RefItem:
845	        tok = self._peek()
846	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
847	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
848	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
849	            return self._parse_qualified_column()
850	        # A quoted identifier, or a bare word not spelled like an aggregate,
851	        # can only be a plain column reference.
852	        if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
853	            self._next()
854	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
855	        func = tok.value.lower()
856	        self._next()  # consume the function name
857	        if not self._accept_op("("):
858	            # e.g. a column literally named "count" -- the name token is
859	            # already consumed, so it is a plain column reference.
860	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
861	        arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted, distinct = self._parse_aggregate_args(func)
862	        self._expect_op(")")
863	        return _RefItem(
864	            "agg",
865	            func=func.upper(),
866	            arg=arg,
867	            distinct=distinct,
868	            arg_table=arg_table,
869	            arg_table_quoted=arg_table_quoted,
870	        )
871	
872	    def _parse_aggregate_args(self, func: str) -> tuple:
873	        # Exactly one argument: '*' for COUNT, otherwise one (possibly
874	        # table-qualified) identifier, optionally preceded by DISTINCT.
875	        # Returns (name, table, table_quoted, distinct); name "" stands
876	        # for '*'.  DISTINCT only deduplicates the argument values of this
877	        # call; it accepts a single column reference only, and any other
878	        # use (a star, a missing argument, an expression, extra arguments
879	        # or a nested call) is a syntax error raised before any file is
880	        # opened.
881	        tok = self._peek()
882	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
883	            raise QueryValidationError(
884	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not a CASE expression"
885	            )
886	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "distinct":
887	            self._next()
888	            tok = self._peek()
889	            if tok.kind == "star":
890	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
891	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) does not accept '*'"
892	                )
893	            if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
894	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
895	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) requires one column argument, "
896	                    f"got {tok.text!r}"
897	                )
898	            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
899	                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
900	                name, table, table_quoted = item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted
901	            else:
902	                self._next()
903	                name, table, table_quoted = tok.value, None, False
904	            nxt = self._peek()
905	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
906	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
907	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) argument must be a column name, "
908	                    "not a function call"
909	                )
910	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
911	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
912	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) argument must be a column "
913	                    "reference, not an expression"
914	                )
915	            return (name, table, table_quoted, True)
916	        if tok.kind == "star":
917	            if func != "count":
918	                raise QuerySyntaxError(f"{func.upper()} does not accept '*'")
919	            self._next()
920	            return ("", None, False, False)
921	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
922	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
923	                f"{func.upper()} requires one column argument, got {tok.text!r}"
924	            )
925	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
926	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
927	            nxt = self._peek()
928	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
929	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
930	                    f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
931	                )
932	            self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
933	            return (item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted, False)
934	        self._next()
935	        nxt = self._peek()
936	        if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
937	            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES:
938	                raise QueryValidationError(
939	                    f"aggregate functions must not be nested: "

1172	    def _parse_arith(self) -> tuple:
1173	        node = self._parse_term()
1174	        while True:
1175	            tok = self._peek()
1176	            if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
1177	                self._next()

1182	    def _parse_term(self) -> tuple:
1183	        node = self._parse_factor()
1184	        while True:
1185	            tok = self._peek()
1186	            if tok.kind == "star":
1187	                self._next()
1188	                node = ("arith", "*", node, self._parse_factor())
1189	            elif tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == "/":
1190	                self._next()
1191	                node = ("arith", "/", node, self._parse_factor())
1192	            else:
1193	                return node

1195	    def _parse_factor(self) -> tuple:
1196	        tok = self._peek()
1197	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
1198	            negate = tok.value == "-"
1199	            self._next()

1202	                # A signed numeric literal is folded at parse time so the

1204	                # (-9223372036854775808 is valid, the bare magnitude is not).

1209	                        value = -value
1210	                    if not (-(2**63) <= value <= 2**63 - 1):
1211	                        raise QuerySyntaxError(
1212	                            "integer literal is outside the int64 range"
1213	                        )

1219	                nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "("

1223	                )

1227	            node[0] == "literal"
1228	            and isinstance(node[1], int)

1237	    def _parse_atom(self) -> tuple:

1256	            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
1257	                item = self._parse_qualified_column()

1261	                tok.kind == "ident"

1275	    def _parse_case(self) -> tuple:
1276	        # A searched CASE: at least one "WHEN cond THEN result", an optional
1277	        # "ELSE result", terminated by END.  Conditions are boolean
1278	        # expressions; results are scalar (numeric, bool or utf8) and may

1281	        branches: list[tuple] = []
1282	        while True:
1283	            self._expect_keyword("when")

1285	            self._expect_keyword("then")
1286	            result = self._parse_arith()
1287	            branches.append((condition, result))
1288	            tok = self._peek()
1289	            if not (tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "when"):
1290	                break
1291	        else_node = None
1292	        if self._accept_keyword("else"):

1294	        self._expect_keyword("end")

1301

1303	        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
1304	        self.pos += 1
1305	        return tok

1316	            self.pos += 1
1317	            return True
1318	        return False
1319	
1320	    def _accept_keyword(self, value: str) -> bool:
1321	        tok = self._peek()

1416	def _bind_plain(select: _Select, schema: Schema, where) -> dict:
1417	    # Non-aggregate path: '*' or a comma-separated list of plain columns and
1418	    # computed scalar expressions (each named with AS).
1419	    bound_items: list[_BoundItem] = []
1420	    if select.star:
1421	        for i, col in enumerate(schema.columns):
1422	            bound_items.append(
1423	                _BoundItem(
1424	                    "column",
1425	                    output_name=col.name,
1426	                    col_index=i,
1427	                    out_type=col.type,
1428	                    nullable=col.nullable,
1429	                )
1430	            )
1431	    else:
1432	        output_seen: set[str] = set()
1433	        for item in select.items:
1434	            if item.kind == "star":
1435	                # A star mixed into a plain projection remains grammatical.
1436	                raise QuerySyntaxError("'*' cannot be mixed with other projection items")
1437	            if item.kind == "column":
1438	                name = item.name
1439	                if name in output_seen:
1440	                    raise QueryValidationError(
1441	                        f"duplicate column in projection: {name!r}"
1442	                    )
1443	                try:
1444	                    col_index = schema.index(name)
1445	                except KeyError:
1446	                    raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown column: {name!r}") from None
1447	                col = schema.columns[col_index]
1448	                output_seen.add(col.name)
1449	                bound_items.append(
1450	                    _BoundItem(
1451	                        "column",
1452	                        output_name=col.name,
1453	                        col_index=col_index,
1454	                        out_type=col.type,
1455	                        nullable=col.nullable,
1456	                    )
1457	                )
1458	            else:  # "expr"
1459	                expr = _bind_expr(item.expr, schema)
1460	                out_type = _expr_type(expr)

1462	                # expression may additionally yield bool or utf8 results
1463	                # (its own WHEN/ELSE type consistency is checked at binding).
1464	                if expr[0] == "case":

1466	                else:
1467	                    allowed_types = ("int64", "float64")
1468	                if out_type not in allowed_types:
1469	                    raise QueryValidationError(
1470	                        f"SELECT expression must be numeric, got {out_type}"
1471	                    )
1472	                alias = item.name
1473	                if alias in output_seen:
1474	                    raise QueryValidationError(f"duplicate result column: {alias!r}")
1475	                output_seen.add(alias)
1476	                bound_items.append(
1477	                    _BoundItem(
1478	                        "expr",
1479	                        output_name=alias,
1480	                        expr=expr,
1481	                        out_type=out_type,

1483	                    )

1487	    }

1494	        "items": tuple(bound_items),
1495	        "aggregates": (),

1498	        "order_by": order_by,
1499	        "distinct": select.distinct,
1500	    }

1517	        if name in order_seen:
1518	            raise QueryValidationError(
1519	                f"duplicate column in ORDER BY: {name!r}"
1520	            )
1521	        order_seen.add(name)
1522	        nulls_first = item.nulls_first if item.nulls_first is not None else False
1523	        if distinct:
1524	            # A DISTINCT query sorts its deduplicated result rows, so every
1525	            # ORDER BY name must be one of the projected outputs (a bare
1526	            # projected column or an explicit AS alias).
1527	            if name not in projected:
1528	                try:
1529	                    schema.index(name)
1530	                except KeyError:
1531	                    raise QueryValidationError(
1532	                        f"unknown ORDER BY column: {name!r}"
1533	                    ) from None
1534	                raise QueryValidationError(
1535	                    f"ORDER BY column {name!r} is not part of the SELECT DISTINCT results"
1536	                )
1537	            bound.append(("out", projected[name], item.descending, nulls_first))
1538	            continue
1539	        # A SELECT alias shadows an input column of the same name.
1540	        if name in aliases:
1541	            bound.append(("expr", aliases[name], item.descending, nulls_first))
1542	            continue
1543	        try:
1544	            col_index = schema.index(name)
1545	        except KeyError:
1546	            raise QueryValidationError(
1547	                f"unknown ORDER BY column: {name!r}"
1548	            ) from None
1549	        bound.append(("col", col_index, item.descending, nulls_first))
1550	    return tuple(bound)
1551	
1552	
1553	def _bind_aggregate(select: _Select, schema: Schema, where) -> dict:
1554	    if select.star:
1555	        raise QueryValidationError("'*' cannot be combined with aggregates or GROUP BY")
1556	
1557	    if (
1558	        select.having is not None
1559	        and select.group_by is None
1560	        and not select.has_aggregate
1561	        and not _having_tree_has_aggregate(select.having)
1562	    ):
1563	        # HAVING filters formed groups; without aggregation or GROUP BY the
1564	        # statement stays a non-aggregate query and HAVING has no meaning.
1565	        raise QueryValidationError(
1566	            "HAVING is only valid with GROUP BY or an aggregate"
1567	        )
1568	
1569	    # Resolve GROUP BY columns first: order matters for the grouping key, and
1570	    # duplicates / unknown columns are rejected here.  Entries are
1571	    # (table, table_quoted, name) triples; names reaching the binder are
1572	    # already canonical (single-file queries never carry a qualifier).
1573	    group_indices: list[int] = []
1574	    group_seen: set[str] = set()

1576	        if name in group_seen:
1577	            raise QueryValidationError(f"duplicate column in GROUP BY: {name!r}")
1578	        group_seen.add(name)
1579	        try:
1580	            group_indices.append(schema.index(name))
1581	        except KeyError:
1582	            raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown GROUP BY column: {name!r}") from None
1583	    group_index_set = set(group_indices)

1585	    # One registry of distinct aggregates shared by SELECT, HAVING and ORDER
1586	    # BY, keyed by (function, argument index, DISTINCT flag) and kept in
1587	    # first-reference order.  HAVING-only aggregates are computed but never
1588	    # projected.
1589	    agg_registry: dict[tuple, int] = {}
1590	    agg_order: list[_BoundItem] = []

1592	    def require_aggregate(func: str, arg_name: str, distinct: bool = False) -> int:
1593	        arg_index, arg_col, label, out_type, nullable = _resolve_agg_call(
1594	            func, arg_name, schema, distinct
1595	        )
1596	        key = (func, arg_index, distinct)
1597	        slot = agg_registry.get(key)
1598	        if slot is None:
1599	            slot = len(agg_order)
1600	            agg_registry[key] = slot
1601	            agg_order.append(
1602	                _BoundItem(
1603	                    "agg",
1604	                    output_name=label,
1605	                    func=func,
1606	                    arg_index=arg_index,
1607	                    arg_type=arg_col.type if arg_col is not None else "",
1608	                    distinct=distinct,
1609	                    out_type=out_type,
1610	                    nullable=nullable,
1611	                )
1612	            )
1613	        return slot
1614	
1615	    # Resolve the projection.  Plain columns must be grouped; output names
1616	    # (group column names and canonical "FUNC(arg)" labels) must be unique.
1617	    bound_items: list[_BoundItem] = []
1618	    output_seen: set[str] = set()
1619	    has_plain = False
1620	    for item in select.items:
1621	        if item.kind == "star":
1622	            raise QueryValidationError(
1623	                "'*' cannot be combined with aggregates or GROUP BY"
1624	            )
1625	        if item.kind == "expr":
1626	            raise QueryValidationError(
1627	                "scalar expressions are not supported in aggregate queries"
1628	            )
1629	        if item.kind == "column":
1630	            has_plain = True
1631	            name = item.name
1632	            try:
1633	                col_index = schema.index(name)
1634	            except KeyError:
1635	                raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown column: {name!r}") from None
1636	            if col_index not in group_index_set:
1637	                raise QueryValidationError(
1638	                    f"column {name!r} must appear in GROUP BY or be wrapped in an aggregate"
1639	                )
1640	            label = name
1641	            if label in output_seen:
1642	                raise QueryValidationError(f"duplicate result column: {name!r}")
1643	            output_seen.add(label)
1644	            col = schema.columns[col_index]
1645	            bound_items.append(
1646	                _BoundItem(
1647	                    "column",
1648	                    output_name=label,
1649	                    col_index=col_index,
1650	                    out_type=col.type,
1651	                    nullable=col.nullable,
1652	                )
1653	            )
1654	        else:
1655	            slot = require_aggregate(item.func, item.arg, item.distinct)
1656	            agg_item = agg_order[slot]
1657	            if agg_item.output_name in output_seen:
1658	                raise QueryValidationError(
1659	                    f"duplicate result column: {agg_item.output_name!r}"
1660	                )
1661	            output_seen.add(agg_item.output_name)
1662	            bound_items.append(agg_item)
1663	
1664	    if select.group_by is None and has_plain:
1665	        # No grouping: every projected column must be an aggregate.
1666	        raise QueryValidationError(
1667	            "without GROUP BY, the projection may contain aggregates only"
1668	        )
1669	
1670	    # HAVING filters the formed groups; it may reuse projected aggregates and
1671	    # may introduce further aggregates that never reach the projection.
1672	    having = None
1673	    if select.having is not None:
1674	        having = _bind_having(
1675	            select.having, schema, group_index_set, agg_order, require_aggregate
1676	        )

1680	        select.order_by, bound_items, schema

1682	    return {
1683	        "mode": "aggregate",
1684	        "group_indices": tuple(group_indices),
1685	        "items": tuple(bound_items),
1686	        "aggregates": tuple(agg_order),
1687	        "where": where,
1688	        "having": having,
1689	        "order_by": order_by,
1690	        "distinct": False,
1691	    }

1694	def _having_tree_has_aggregate(node: tuple) -> bool:
1695	    """Whether a parsed (unbound) HAVING tree names at least one aggregate."""
1696	    tag = node[0]
1697	    if tag == "hagg":
1698	        return True
1699	    if tag in ("literal", "column"):
1700	        return False
1701	    if tag in ("not", "isnull"):
1702	        return _having_tree_has_aggregate(node[1])
1703	    if tag == "cmp":
1704	        return _having_tree_has_aggregate(node[2]) or _having_tree_has_aggregate(
1705	            node[3]
1706	        )
1707	    return _having_tree_has_aggregate(node[1]) or _having_tree_has_aggregate(node[2])

1709	
1710	def _bind_having(
1711	    node: tuple,
1712	    schema: Schema,
1713	    group_index_set: set[int],
1714	    agg_order: list[_BoundItem],
1715	    require_aggregate,
1716	) -> tuple:
1717	    tag = node[0]
1718	    if tag == "literal":
1719	        return node
1720	    if tag == "column":
1721	        name = node[1]
1722	        try:
1723	            col_index = schema.index(name)
1724	        except KeyError:
1725	            raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown column: {name!r}") from None
1726	        if col_index not in group_index_set:
1727	            raise QueryValidationError(
1728	                f"HAVING column {name!r} must appear in GROUP BY or be wrapped in an aggregate"
1729	            )

1731	        return ("column", name, col_index, col.type, col.nullable)
1732	    if tag == "hagg":
1733	        slot = require_aggregate(node[1], node[2], node[5])
1734	        agg_item = agg_order[slot]
1735	        return ("hagg", slot, agg_item.out_type, agg_item.nullable)
1736	    if tag == "not":
1737	        operand = _bind_having(
1738	            node[1], schema, group_index_set, agg_order, require_aggregate
1739	        )
1740	        _require_having_boolean(operand, "NOT")
1741	        return ("not", operand)
1742	    if tag in ("and", "or"):
1743	        left = _bind_having(
1744	            node[1], schema, group_index_set, agg_order, require_aggregate
1745	        )
1746	        right = _bind_having(
1747	            node[2], schema, group_index_set, agg_order, require_aggregate
1748	        )

1750	        _require_having_boolean(right, tag.upper())
1751	        return (tag, left, right)
1752	    if tag == "isnull":
1753	        operand = _bind_having(
1754	            node[1], schema, group_index_set, agg_order, require_aggregate
1755	        )
1756	        if operand[0] not in ("literal", "column", "hagg"):
1757	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
1758	                "IS NULL operand must be a group column, an aggregate or a literal"
1759	            )

1761	    if tag == "cmp":
1762	        op = node[1]
1763	        left = _bind_having(
1764	            node[2], schema, group_index_set, agg_order, require_aggregate
1765	        )
1766	        right = _bind_having(
1767	            node[3], schema, group_index_set, agg_order, require_aggregate
1768	        )
1769	        if left[0] not in ("literal", "column", "hagg") or right[0] not in (
1770	            "literal",
1771	            "column",
1772	            "hagg",
1773	        ):
1774	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
1775	                "comparison operands must be group columns, aggregates or literals"
1776	            )
1777	        left_t = _having_value_type(left)
1778	        right_t = _having_value_type(right)
1779	        if "bool" in (left_t, right_t):
1780	            if left_t != "bool" or right_t != "bool":
1781	                raise QueryValidationError(
1782	                    f"bool can only be compared to bool, got {left_t} and {right_t}"
1783	                )

1787	            if left_t != "utf8" or right_t != "utf8":
1788	                raise QueryValidationError(
1789	                    f"utf8 can only be compared to utf8, got {left_t} and {right_t}"
1790	                )

1794	            )
1795	        return ("cmp", op, left, right)
1796	    raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unsupported expression: {tag}")  # pragma: no cover - defensive
1797	
1798	
1799	def _having_value_type(node: tuple) -> str:
1800	    """The static value type of a bound HAVING leaf."""
1801	    tag = node[0]
1802	    if tag == "literal":
1803	        return node[2]
1804	    if tag == "column":

"""Single-file SQL query layer.

Public API:

* :func:`query_file` -- run a ``SELECT ... FROM input [WHERE ...]`` query
  against one columnar file and return a :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.Table`
* :func:`query_files` -- run a statement against a table-name to path
  mapping, optionally chaining several equi-joins
* :func:`explain_file` / :func:`explain_files` -- parse, bind and plan the
  same statements without executing them; only file metadata is read
* :class:`QuerySyntaxError` -- lexical / grammatical errors
* :class:`QueryValidationError` -- unknown columns, wrong table name,
  type-incompatible comparisons, invalid aggregate use

The accepted grammar (keywords case-insensitive)::

    query       := SELECT [DISTINCT] select_item (',' select_item)*
                   FROM ident [WHERE expr] [GROUP BY ident (',' ident)*]
                   [HAVING expr]
                   [ORDER BY order_item (',' order_item)*]
                   [LIMIT uint]
    select_item := '*' | ident | agg_name '(' [DISTINCT] ('*' | ident) ')'
                   | scalar_expr AS alias
    order_item  := (ident | agg_name '(' [DISTINCT] ('*' | ident) ')')
                   [ASC | DESC] [NULLS FIRST | NULLS LAST]
    expr       := or_expr
    or_expr     := and_expr (OR and_expr)*
    and_expr    := cmp_expr (AND cmp_expr)*
    cmp_expr    := not_factor (cmp_op not_factor)?
    not_factor  := NOT not_factor | postfix
    postfix     := scalar_expr (IS [NOT] NULL)?
    scalar_expr := term (('+' | '-') term)*
    term        := factor (('*' | '/') factor)*
    factor      := ('+' | '-') factor | atom
    atom        := '(' expr ')' | operand
                | CASE WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr
                  (WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr)*
                  (ELSE scalar_expr)? END
    operand     := ident | literal
    literal     := TRUE | FALSE | [+-]? int64 | [+-]? finite float64
                   | single-quoted utf8

The supported aggregates are ``COUNT(*)``, ``COUNT(ident)`` and
``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` applied to one column.  Each of
``COUNT`` / ``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` also accepts
``DISTINCT`` before its single column argument (``COUNT(DISTINCT ident)``
etc.): rows are first selected by WHERE, then within each group (or the
single global group) NULL arguments are ignored and the remaining values
are deduplicated by the column's type -- float64 ``0.0`` and ``-0.0``
count as the same value -- before the aggregate runs.  ``COUNT(DISTINCT
x)`` returns the number of distinct non-NULL values (0 on empty input,
a non-nullable int64); the other DISTINCT aggregates return NULL when no
distinct non-NULL value remains and otherwise keep the result type,
nullability, comparison rules and overflow / non-finite
:class:`QueryValidationError` behaviour of their plain counterparts.
DISTINCT here only deduplicates the aggregate's argument values; it does
not change ``SELECT DISTINCT`` row deduplication, and the argument stays
a single column reference (no ``*``, expressions, multiple arguments or
nested aggregates).  A misplaced DISTINCT keyword, a missing argument,
``*``, an expression or multiple arguments inside a DISTINCT call raise
:class:`QuerySyntaxError` before any file is opened.  DISTINCT
aggregates may appear wherever plain aggregates may (SELECT, HAVING,
ORDER BY), and textually identical calls share one computation.  Without
GROUP BY the projection may contain aggregate expressions only; with
GROUP BY it may additionally contain the grouped columns.  A bare ``*``
must not be mixed with aggregates or grouping.  Aggregates are not
allowed inside WHERE, may not be nested, and aliases are not supported
for bare columns or aggregate calls.

Scalar arithmetic (parentheses, unary ``+``/``-``, binary ``+`` ``-``
``*`` ``/``; precedence: parentheses, unary, ``*``/``/``, ``+``/``-``)
is available over int64 / float64 columns and numeric literals in SELECT
and WHERE.  A computed SELECT expression must be named with ``AS`` (the
alias follows the usual identifier rules and must be unique among the
output names); bare columns and aggregate calls keep their existing
result names.  int64 ``+``/``-``/``*`` on two int64 operands yields
int64; any float64 operand or a division yields float64, and unary
operators preserve the operand type.  Any NULL operand makes the result
NULL; the output column is nullable iff a participating column is
nullable (pure constants are not).  int64 overflow, division by zero and
non-finite float64 results raise :class:`QueryValidationError`.  A
numeric expression used directly as a boolean condition is rejected with
:class:`QueryValidationError` as well.  Non-aggregate queries execute
WHERE, then compute the sort keys, stably sort, apply LIMIT and only
then evaluate the SELECT expressions, so filtered or truncated rows
never trigger division-by-zero or overflow in the projection; a
DISTINCT query instead evaluates the projection right after WHERE,
deduplicates the result rows, and only then sorts and applies LIMIT.  ORDER BY
may name a SELECT alias (an alias shadows an input column of the same
name) and sorts on the expression's result type with the usual NULL
placement and stability rules.  Aggregate queries do not accept scalar
expressions: GROUP BY keys and aggregate arguments stay plain column
references, and mixing a scalar expression into an aggregate query
raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.

``SELECT DISTINCT`` removes duplicate rows from a non-aggregate query:
the projection may be a star, plain columns or ``AS``-aliased scalar
expressions exactly as without DISTINCT, and deduplication compares the
full projected result row column by column after WHERE.  Two NULLs in
the same result column compare equal, NULL never equals a non-NULL
value, bool / utf8 / numeric values keep their existing comparison
semantics, and float64 ``0.0`` and ``-0.0`` compare equal.  Without
ORDER BY the surviving rows keep the order of the first occurrence of
each distinct result row; ORDER BY then sorts the deduplicated rows and
LIMIT keeps the first N.  The projection expressions are evaluated
only for rows that passed WHERE (and, with ORDER BY, before the sort),
so a division by zero, int64 overflow or non-finite float64 result that
actually occurs still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.  ORDER BY
of a DISTINCT query may name only bare columns or explicit aliases that
are part of the projection; an unprojected or otherwise unknown name
raises :class:`QueryValidationError`, and the sort direction, NULL
placement and stability rules are unchanged.  DISTINCT combined with
GROUP BY, HAVING or any aggregate projection raises
:class:`QueryValidationError`; argument-level ``DISTINCT`` inside an
aggregate call (``COUNT(DISTINCT ...)`` etc.) is a separate feature
described above and stays an aggregate query.  A missing projection, a
repeated DISTINCT or a misplaced DISTINCT keyword raises
:class:`QuerySyntaxError` before any file is opened.

Searched CASE expressions
(``CASE WHEN cond THEN result [WHEN ...] [ELSE result] END``; the simple
``CASE value WHEN ...`` form is not supported and at least one WHEN is
required) are scalar operands and may be nested inside more arithmetic,
comparisons and other CASE expressions.  For each row the WHEN conditions
are tested in written order and only TRUE matches; FALSE and UNKNOWN fall
through, an explicit ELSE supplies the fallback and a missing ELSE yields
NULL.  Only the chosen result is evaluated, so division by zero, int64
overflow or a non-finite float64 inside an unhit branch never raises; a
chosen result that errors still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
Every reachable THEN and an explicit ELSE must share one type family:
int64 and float64 may mix and unify to float64, while bool and utf8 must
match each other exactly (any other mix raises
:class:`QueryValidationError`).  The result column is nullable if any
reachable result is nullable or the ELSE is omitted.  WHEN conditions use
the same boolean type check and three-valued logic as WHERE; CASE stays a
scalar expression, so it is rejected in aggregate arguments, GROUP BY and
the projection of an aggregate query just like the other scalar
expressions.

Operator precedence (highest first) is NOT, comparison, AND, OR; IS [NOT]
NULL is a postfix of its scalar operand.  Comparison operands may be
column references, literals or scalar arithmetic expressions.  WHERE
follows SQL three-valued logic: a normal
comparison against NULL yields UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN propagates through the
logical operators, and only TRUE rows are returned.

After WHERE, rows are grouped in GROUP BY column order (a NULL key forms
its own group); without an explicit ORDER BY groups come out in the order
of their first selected row.  An optional HAVING clause between GROUP BY
and ORDER BY filters the formed groups with the same boolean expression
grammar and three-valued logic as WHERE: its conditions combine grouping
columns, aggregate calls and type-compatible literals with NOT / AND / OR
/ comparisons / IS [NOT] NULL, only groups whose condition is TRUE are
kept, and aggregates named in HAVING need not appear in SELECT.  Without
GROUP BY HAVING filters the single global aggregate row (still produced
when WHERE selected no rows); with GROUP BY an empty selection yields
zero groups.  HAVING may not name ungrouped plain columns, ``*``, CASE,
scalar arithmetic or nested aggregates; it is rejected on a completely
non-aggregate query.  ORDER BY may only name a selected result; ASC is the
default, NULLs sort last regardless of direction unless NULLS FIRST /
NULLS LAST is given, and groups equal on every sort key keep that
first-row order.  LIMIT then keeps the first N groups.  Without GROUP BY
and aggregates an aggregate query over zero selected rows still yields one
output row (COUNT 0, the other aggregates NULL), unless HAVING removes it;
with GROUP BY it yields zero rows.

Multi-file queries (:func:`query_files`) add a deterministic chain of zero
or more equi-joins to the grammar::

    query := SELECT ... FROM from_table
             { join_kind JOIN next_table
               ON (earlier_table.col = next_table.col
                   | next_table.col = earlier_table.col) } ...
    join_kind := INNER | LEFT | RIGHT | FULL OUTER

``sources`` maps table names to file paths; only the tables referenced by
the statement are read.  Each join step introduces exactly one not-yet-used
table (aliases and repeated tables are rejected) and its single ON equality
connects a qualified column of that new table with a qualified column of any
table introduced earlier (FROM or a previous join); the two sides of the
equality are interchangeable.  Compound or non-equality ON conditions,
other join types and ``FULL`` without ``OUTER`` are syntax errors raised
before any file is opened.  In any statement that contains a JOIN every
column reference outside ``COUNT(*)`` must be qualified as ``table.column``
(either part may be a double-quoted identifier).  ``SELECT *`` emits the
referenced schemas in FROM/JOIN order with ``table.column`` names; explicit
projections keep their qualified names and aggregates keep the uppercase
``FUNC(table.column)`` labels.

Each step is evaluated with the materialised intermediate result as its
left input and the newly read table as its right input.  Join keys may
share a type or mix int64 with float64; NULL keys never match.  INNER JOIN
emits every matching combination, LEFT JOIN also emits unmatched left rows
with the right-side values set to NULL (the new table's result columns are
nullable), RIGHT JOIN emits all new-table rows in new-file order (one new
row's matches expand in intermediate/current row order) padding the whole
intermediate side with NULL (every earlier table's result columns become
nullable), and FULL OUTER JOIN emits the LEFT JOIN output and then appends
the unmatched new rows in new-file order (every result column is nullable).
INNER / LEFT / FULL expand in the current intermediate row order, with the
matching new rows in new-file order within one current row; RIGHT expands
in new-file row order with the matches in current row order.  Nullability
is derived per step: once a step makes an earlier table's columns
nullable, later steps keep them nullable.  WHERE / GROUP BY / HAVING /
projection / DISTINCT / stable sorting / LIMIT run only after the whole
chain has been built, with their usual semantics.

The multi-file entry points (:func:`query_files`, :func:`explain_files`)
take an optional ``join_strategy`` of ``"hash"`` or ``"sort_merge"``; an
explicit strategy is applied to every join step.  Both strategies accept
the same statements and return identical column descriptions, values, NULL
placement and row order; they differ only in how matching right rows are
located (a right-key hash index versus sorting both sides on the key and
merging equal-key runs).  With the argument omitted the historical
default join path is used and the explain plan carries no strategy field;
with an explicit strategy every plan Join operator gains a ``strategy``
field of ``HASH`` or ``SORT_MERGE``.  A JOIN-less statement accepts either
strategy but gains no extra operator, and an invalid strategy raises
:class:`ValueError` before any source file is opened.

The explain plan lists the referenced sources and their Scan operators in
FROM/JOIN order with ``required_columns`` attributed to each source, then
one Join operator per step in the same order, recording the step type and
the two normalised qualified keys (the earlier table on the left, the
freshly introduced table on the right).

Row-group-partitioned (v2) files are read selectively: every query decodes
only the column blocks its plan actually references (a join chain
additionally reads each table's ON keys), and single-file statements --
:func:`query_file` and JOIN-less :func:`query_files` -- push the
AND-connected, type-compatible comparisons and IS [NOT] NULL conditions of
WHERE down to the per-group statistics.  A row group is skipped only when
its statistics prove the pushed condition can never be TRUE for any of its
rows; OR, NOT, CASE, arithmetic, column-to-column comparisons and
undecidable ranges keep the group, and surviving rows are still filtered
row by row with the full WHERE condition.  When every group is excluded
the statement simply sees zero rows, so empty results, ``COUNT(*)``, other
global aggregates and HAVING keep their usual semantics.  Both format
versions return identical column descriptions, values, row order, sorting,
LIMIT, join and export results for the same data and statement.  In the
explain plan a v2 single-source Scan operator additionally carries
``row_groups_total``, ``row_groups_selected`` and ``pushed_condition``
(the pushed-down subset of the WHERE condition as a condition tree, or
null); v1 plans are unchanged.
"""

_KEYWORDS = frozenset(
    (
        "select",
        "distinct",
        "from",
        "where",
        "as",
        "not",
        "and",
        "or",
        "is",
        "null",
        "true",
        "false",

        "asc",

        "else",
